'''Raymond Hide''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS}} (17 May 1929 – 6 September 2016) was a British physicist, who was a professor of physics at the [[University of Oxford]] and, since 2000, senior research investigator at [[Imperial College, London]].

==Education ==
Hide was educated at [[Percy Jackson Grammar School]], near [[Doncaster]], [[South Yorkshire]]<ref>Admissions Registers. Percy Jackson GS Collection, Doncaster Archives</ref> and the [[University of Manchester]], where he obtained a first-class degree in physics in 1950.  He then went to [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]] and studied for a PhD in the [[Geophysics]] Department, he was awarded a doctorate in 1953. 

== Career ==
After research at the [[University of Chicago]], he was a senior research fellow at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] at [[Harwell, Oxfordshire]] from 1954 to 1957.  He was a lecturer in physics at [[King's College, Newcastle]] from 1957 to 1961, before becoming professor of geophysics and physics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1961 to 1967).  He was then head of the Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Lab at the [[Met Office]] (1967 to 1990). He won the [[Chree medal and prize]] in 1975. He was appointed a [[Oxbridge Fellow|fellow]] of [[Jesus College, Oxford]] in 1983, holding his fellowship until 1996; he was then appointed an honorary fellow in 1997.  Between 1984 and 1990, he was the [[Gresham Professor of Astronomy|professor of astronomy]] at [[Gresham College]], based central London.<ref>[http://www.gresham.ac.uk/gresham-professor-of-astronomy List of Gresham Astronomy Professors and their lectures on the Gresham College website] (accessed 19 November 2013)</ref> He was director of the Robert Hooke Institute and a visiting professor in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1990 to 1992.

His research covered geophysics ([[geomagnetism]], [[meteorology]], [[geodesy]], [[oceanography]]), [[planetary physics]], geophysical fluid mechanics, including [[magnetohydrodynamics]] (MHD), and [[nonlinear systems]]. His work on the hydrodynamics and MHD of spinning fluids defined flow phenomena in atmospheres and oceans and the interiors of planetary bodies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rmets.org/professor-raymond-hide-cbe|title=Professor Raymond Hide CBE|publisher=Royal Meteorological Society|access-date=27 November 2016|archive-date=6 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106023031/https://www.rmets.org/professor-raymond-hide-cbe|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hide was elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1964 and a [[fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1971.<ref name="Bio_RS">{{Cite journal|last=Read|first=P. L.|date=2019|title=Raymond Hide. 17 May 1929—6 September 2016|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=67|pages=191–215|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2019.0016|s2cid=201098259|doi-access=free}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize]] in 1982, the [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society]] for geophysics in 1989, the [[William Bowie Medal]] by the [[American Geophysical Union]] in 1997,<ref>{{cite journal| url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1029/97EO00195|doi= 10.1029/97EO00195|title=Hide Receives the Bowie Medal |date= 1997| access-date=25 October 2024|last1= Dickey|first1= Jean O.|last2= Hide|first2= Raymond|journal= Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union|volume= 78|issue= 29|pages= 295–296}}</ref> the Royal Society's [[Hughes Medal]] in 1998,  [[Lewis Fry Richardson#Legacy|Lewis Fry Richardson Medal]] by the [[European Geosciences Union]] in 1999<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/lewis-fry-richardson/1999/raymond-hide/| title=Lewis Fry Richardson Medal 1999: Raymond Hide |access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref>  and the [[Royal Meteorological Society]]'s [[Symons Gold Medal]] in 2002.

He was appointed [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in 1990. He served as president of the [[Royal Meteorological Society]] from 1974 to 1976 and was a member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]], having been appointed by [[Pope John Paul II]] in 1996.

In 2000 he became senior research investigator, at the Department of Mathematics, [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U20075| title=Hide, Prof. Raymond|work=[[Who's Who|Who's Who 2008]]| publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|date=December 2007 |access-date=2008-10-05}}</ref> He died on 6 September 2016 at the age of 87.<ref name="DeathRMS">{{cite web |url=https://www.rmets.org/professor-raymond-hide-cbe |title=Professor Raymond Hide CBE |work=News |publisher=[[Royal Meteorological Society]] |date=2016-09-08 |access-date=2016-09-08 |archive-date=6 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106023031/https://www.rmets.org/professor-raymond-hide-cbe |url-status=dead }}</ref>
